trajectory_summary: The call opens with a shaky, garbled intro but the customer is genuinely interested and cooperative throughout — confirming address, tenure, roof age, bill pain, and even disclosing veteran/fixed-income status. The call collapses at the finish line: rather than routing the unknown-credit-score customer to the closer or credit pull, the rep unilaterally advises him to wait, and the customer immediately asks to be removed from the call list.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear; this should be scored as dq (self-inflicted) rather than any positive outcome — the rep manufactured the disqualification by telling the customer to wait rather than letting the closer's credit pull decide, per qualifiers.credit_qualifier.spencer_operator_note. This is very likely a lost sit, not a neutral non-event.

observed_outcome.quote: Well, yeah, if I were you, Irvin, I would wait to look into solar until you know that your credit is above $6.70.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep disqualifies the customer on a self-reported 'I don't know' about credit, advising him to wait, and the customer responds by asking to be removed from the call list — no appointment was set and the call ended as a rep-driven disqualification.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the $400 bill and acknowledged it ('We'll definitely help you get that cut down') but immediately moved to the credit qualifier rather than using the bill pain as leverage against the eventual credit-based disqualification; the flip should have gone at 01:57 to tie the bill pain to urgency before the credit question derailed the call.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The call ended at the credit qualifier stage before the rep ever reached bill-collection; no request for the physical utility bill (text/email/photo) occurred.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep asked what got the customer interested and got a clear answer (save money, high bills), acknowledged it briefly ('Yeah. We can definitely help you get your bills cut down.') but never circled back to this stated motivation when the credit issue arose — the bill-pain reason could have been used to justify continuing forward (e.g., to a closer) rather than telling him to wait.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Self-DQ on unknown/stated credit instead of routing to closer's pull
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Well, yeah, if I were you, Irvin, I would wait to look into solar until you know that your credit is above $6.70.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This single line converts a cooperative, qualified-sounding lead ($400 bill, decent roof, veteran discount interest) into an immediate opt-out request. Per qualifiers.credit_qualifier's operator note, stated/unknown credit should not be a setter-level DQ trigger — this is the costliest moment in the call and the one most within the rep's control to fix.

key_moments.quote: This is calling with Ion. I got a request to look at a disclaimer for your line. How are you interested? Have a veteran discount and you have Tesla
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep never states their own name clearly and the phrase 'disclaimer for your line' does not map to any coherent lead-source explanation, leaving legitimacy unestablished at the open.

A $400/month bill was captured cleanly as a strong pain point, but the rep's reaction ('Oh my goodness. 400. Okay. Yeah. We'll definitely help you get that cut down.') acknowledges but does not flip it into alignment-against-the-utility before moving straight to the credit qualifier.

key_moments.quote: I'm a retired disabled veteran and retired Connecticut state employee. So my money is only a certain amount, and I don't know what my credit is doing right now.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer disclosed veteran status, retirement, and fixed income as a vulnerability/trust gift. The rep's only response is 'Mhmm. Okay.' before pivoting straight into the disqualifying credit advice, with no acknowledgment of the disclosure itself.

key_moments.quote: Well, yeah, if I were you, Irvin, I would wait to look into solar until you know that your credit is above $6.70.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep unilaterally disqualifies on a customer's stated 'I have no idea' about credit rather than passing the lead through to a closer/credit pull. Per the schema's spencer_operator_note, stated credit is unreliable and DQ'ing on 'I don't know' (not even a stated low number) is a policy question that should default to letting the closer decide, not the setter killing the lead outright.
